# Independent performance runtime addendum — parallel-sync policy

Verdict: **PASS for the pure policy component at Source 63c88dcf0eb7364521c5ea79b8cd67e63e4990b0**. No blocking performance finding. The complete IDE is not certified by this verdict.

This addendum supplements `performance-review-round1.md`, whose SHA-256 remains `71795b1c303b10a11325ef9e122b731776e7f0ce202823844a3c354fbf95590b`. I read the current Rust implementation, all ten policy tests, the pinned AGP parser and feature ranges, the preserved static review, the actual execution harness, raw logs and runtime-recovery receipts. I executed no Cargo, rustc, tests, Gradle, app, native probe or benchmark, made no Git/source/fixture edits, and spawned no agents. Root owns the execution lease.

## Runtime evidence independently verified

The ordinary locked all-features component run passed **241 tests in eight groups**, with zero failures, ignored, measured or filtered tests. The groups contain 85, 30, 20, 10, 27, 21, 29 and 19 passing tests. All eight executed test targets were freshly compiled, with compiler JSON pointing into `/workspace/android-studio-parallel-sync-policy`; no shared-cache freshness claim was substituted for current-source execution. The raw log explicitly records `long_invalid_input_has_bounded_work_and_error_output ... ok`. SHA-256: `01d4b8e155f9c0e2cdec9fa1562b45c29d7aa7de29c0cc5816ee95a361e4f173`.

The exact `check_supports_parallel_sync` owner capture passed once, with nine other tests filtered and zero ignored. Its nine original assertions remain present and unchanged. Its freshly compiled test target points to the current worktree. Raw log SHA-256: `b1b45f3b1d6d7e3f6ae92ca481a676326cbad7528a408578a44424fe9940fa04`. This owner capture does not grant canonical lead parity credit.

The normal locked all-features library build, repository strict release Clippy and full workspace format check exited zero. I checked the library compiler JSON for a fresh current-worktree library compilation and the Clippy raw command for `--release --all-targets --all-features -- --deny warnings`. Raw log hashes are respectively `18a067ad8f063d8d25f3e040407244e29289f768b53f755f5b9e99f96e1bf0dd`, `374a5f0ae1c5538821077712da269021283d9cd6e7c6ca447eca2b371380500a` and `e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855`.

The recorded whole-command elapsed times are 38.921990292 seconds for component tests, 5.355480633 seconds for the library build, 61.829929091 seconds for strict Clippy, 27.811437709 seconds for formatting and 4.789697501 seconds for the exact original test. These include command/build overhead. They are validation observations, not policy latency, allocation, RSS, scalability or comparative performance benchmarks.

I independently rehashed all **4,717 current source bindings** and all **148 immutable originals**. They match the preserved execution snapshot and rebound guard. Every stage's before/after snapshot is identical, including the exact seven source pathspecs, full index identity and empty recorded Git status. The eight touched compiler roots retain their original bytes and have strictly increased recorded mtimes. At-execution compiler/library file identities remain attached to those raw runs; later legitimate shared-cache replacement is not treated as an implementation change or a failed gate.

The retained ten-test executable `/tmp/parallel-sync-verified-binaries/parallel-sync-tests10` is 1,762,376 bytes and still hashes to `5867af45da2c75a32f26f9a70453ceaa3efb7d983b04eed6ccb3c1482b1d7ab6`. The execution harness runs each stage synchronously and records a completed exit. The retained closure records no active owned processes, no owner artifact removal, and release of the execution lease to Root. This does not make a statement about other owners' current processes.

## Bounded behavior and remaining limits

The successful policy borrows the captured model, reads a signed scalar producer tuple, and parses only the explicit AGP string. It does not clone descriptions/model vectors, traverse modules, request Gradle work, schedule tasks, introduce caches, lock resources or add UI work. Fixed scalar boundary comparisons remain constant work.

The parser checks the stored UTF-8 byte length before scanning or formatting input. An AGP string longer than 64 bytes returns a fixed literal error without echoing the string. The now-executed 100,000-character case verifies that rejection and short diagnostic; its fixture allocates and copies the test input before the policy call. No test wall-time or allocation budget is claimed from that assertion. Inputs at most 64 bytes are parsed through borrowed substrings and fixed scalar numeric values, giving bounded per-call parsing work. The pinned signed-Int grammar admits at most 40 bytes: three ten-digit components, two dots and an eight-byte `-alphaNN` suffix. The 64-byte guard excludes no successfully parsed reference spelling.

Malformed/unsupported input at or below the cap still allocates a bounded formatted diagnostic. The inherited `CapturedField::available` error path formats or copies arbitrary capability/detail diagnostics and can therefore perform work proportional to those supplied diagnostics. This limitation is unchanged and already called out in the preserved static review. The full public Result/error API is not certified as allocation-free or as having a universal total-memory cap.

Full-app/native behavior, full workspace CI, canonical lead exact parity capture and merge remain pending lead gates. There is no actual parallel Gradle scheduling in this component and no claim of a concurrency speedup, hardware budget, IDE startup time, memory budget or large-project responsiveness. No further fix round is required by this scoped performance review. Suggested .rules additions: none.
